answer: Every prospective agent must dock at the identity jetty by locking a 10,000-token slashable bond and producing remote attestation from a TEE whose manufacturer-fused key is recorded on-chain. The registry bridges that hardware key to one agent identifier and rejects any second registration from the same key, so each fake identity requires a new enclave. An attacker’s cost scales linearly as hardware rental plus full bond per sybil, while the trellis of bonded enclaves gives seizable collateral.
